label: Inoculated against smallpox
description: Jenner was inoculated in the old method as a boy during the mass inoculation.

sources.quote: He, who had been inoculated in the old method as a boy during the mass inoculation at Wootton-under-Edge in 1756, was an inoculator using the Suttonian method before he claimed to have discovered vaccination.

label: Initial cowpox experiments
description: Jenner conducted initial experiments with cowpox.

sources.quote: After a few initial experiments with cowpox in I796 and 1798, Jenner's original vaccine lymph was lost, and it was not until the end of January 1799, when cowpox was discovered in Gray's Inn Lane by Woodville, that experiments were resumed.

label: Cowpox discovered in Gray's Inn Lane
description: Cowpox was discovered by Woodville, allowing experiments to resume.

sources.quote: it was not until the end of January 1799, when cowpox was discovered in Gray's Inn Lane by Woodville, that experiments were resumed.

label: Experiments resumed with Woodville's lymph
description: Jenner operated on twenty persons using lymph from Woodville.

sources.quote: With this lymph, Jenner operated on twenty persons and reported to Woodville: 'Berkely, February 1799. The rise, progress, and termination of the pustules created by the virus were exactly that of the true cowpox.'

label: Wrote letter to Lord Egremont
description: Jenner wrote to his patron regarding vaccine lymph.

sources.quote: At the beginning of i8oo he wrote a letter to Lord Egremont, one of his patrons, who had complained that some of the vaccine sent from London had produced pustular eruptions when used on his family at Petworth.

label: Mass inoculation conducted by Daniel Sutton
description: A mass inoculation was conducted in Maidstone.
